ex.ja: 安月給でどうにか暮らしています。

note.ja: 北欧語 skrapa（こする）から。「こする・削り取る」→ こすれて生じた窮地。skyscraper（空をこするもの）も同じ。

ex.en: Yes, I'll have sherry.

en: Artfully cunning; secretly mischievous; wily.
Dexterous in performing an action, so as to escape notice.

sly.ety:
From Middle English sly, sley, sleigh, sleiȝ, from Old Norse slǿgr (“sly, cunning”, literally “capable of hitting or striking”), from Proto-Germanic *slōgiz (“lively, agile, cunning, sly, striking”), from Proto-Indo-European *slak- (“to hit, throw”).

In all likelihood, however, unrelated with Saterland Frisian slau (“sly, crafty”), Dutch sluw (“sly, cunning”), Low German slu (“sly, cunning”), German schlau (“clever, crafty”). assassinate.ety: From assassin + -ate, after Middle French assassiner.

ex.en: They attempted to assassinate the president.
ex.ja: 彼らは大統領の暗殺を企てた。

ex.en: He was ignorant of the plot to assassinate him.
ex.ja: 彼は自分を暗殺しようという陰謀を知らなかった。

ex.en: The great Roman hero, Julius Caesar, was assassinated.
ex.ja: かのローマの偉大な英雄、ジュリアス・シーザーは暗殺されたのです。

note.ja: assassin（暗殺者）+ -ate。「暗殺する」。

en: One who robs others in a lawless area, especially as part of a group.
An outlaw.
To rob, or steal from, in the manner of a bandit.

bandit.ety: Borrowed from Italian bandito (“outlawed”), a derivative of Italian bandire (“to ban”), from Late Latin bandīre, an alteration (due to Gothic 𐌱𐌰𐌽𐌳𐍅𐌾𐌰𐌽 (bandwjan, “to signal”)) of Late Latin bannīre (“to ban”), from Frankish *bannan (“to ban”). Doublet of bandito.

ex.en: The bandits demanded all money in the register.
ex.ja: 悪漢は金銭登録機のお金を要求した。

ex.en: The bandits made a raid on the village.
ex.ja: 山賊がその村を襲った。

note.ja: イタリア語 bandito（追放された者）から。bandire（追放する）。「山賊」。ban（禁止）と同じ。

en: Having been subject to banishment; kicked out and forbidden from returning; forbidden and prohibited.

ex.en: We banished him from the country.
ex.ja: 我々は彼を国外に追放した。

ex.en: He was banished from the kingdom.
ex.ja: 彼はその王国から追放となった。

ex.en: He was banished to an island for high treason.
ex.ja: 彼は大逆罪で島流しにされた。

en: Wearing nothing on the feet.
Of a vehicle on an icy road: not using snow chains.
Wearing nothing on the feet.
Transmitting without the use of an amplifier.

barefoot.ety: From Middle English barefote, barfot, from Old English bærfōt (“barefoot”), from Proto-West Germanic *baʀafōt, from Proto-Germanic *bazafōts (“barefoot”) equivalent to bare + foot. Cognate with Scots barefit (“barefoot”), Old Frisian berfōt ("barefoot"; modern Saterland Frisian boarfouts (“barefoot”, adverb)), Dutch barrevoets (“barefoot”, adverb), German barfuß (“barefoot”), Danish barfodet (“barefoot”), Swedish barfota (“barefoot”, adverb), Icelandic berfættur (“barefoot”), Yiddish באָרוועס (borves, “barefoot”).

ex.en: I'm always barefoot at home.
ex.ja: 家ではいつも裸足です。

ex.en: I can't walk barefoot.
ex.ja: 裸足では歩けません。

ex.en: Why are you barefoot?
ex.ja: どうして裸足なの？

note.ja: bare（裸の）+ foot（足）。「はだしの」。

en: An artificial obstruction, such as a dam, in a river designed to increase its depth or to divert its flow.
A heavy curtain of artillery fire directed in front of one's own troops to screen and protect them.
To direct a barrage at.

barrage.ety: Unadapted borrowing from French barrage (“barrage, barrier”) c. 1859. Compare barrier.

ex.en: The minister had to face a barrage of questions from the press.
ex.ja: 大臣は新聞記者たちからの矢継ぎ早の質問に直面しなくてはならなかった。

note.ja: フランス語 barrage（せき止めること）から。barre（棒）。「ダム」→ 弾丸で壁を作る →「集中砲火・殺到」。bar と同じ。

en: To apply or make use of (someone or something); to employ, to use.
To impart (something) gratuitously; to present (something) to someone or something, especially as a gift or an honour; to confer, to give…

bestow.ety:
PIE word
 *h₁épi
The verb is derived from Middle English bestowen, bistouen, bistowen (“to give, bestow; to apply (something to something else); to arrange or have control over (something); to place (someone) in a position; to use (for some purpose); (reflexive) to find (oneself) a place to live or shelter”) [and other forms], from bi- (prefix forming verbs, often with a completive, figurative, or intensive meaning) + stouen, stowen (“to pack (cargo) in a ship, stow; to place (someone) in a certain position; to provide quarters for, lodge; etc.”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂- (“

ex.en: They bestowed several gifts on the royal visitors.
ex.ja: 彼らは王室からの訪問者に贈り物を幾つか渡した。

ex.en: He who gives to another bestows on himself.
ex.ja: 情けは人のためならず。

ex.en: The committee bestowed a medal on him.
ex.ja: 委員会は彼にメダルを授けた。

note.ja: be（強意）+ stow（置く）。「置き与える」→「授ける」。

en: The quality of being exceptionally effulgent (giving off light).
The quality of having extraordinary mental capacity.

ex.en: Every time I saw him, I was overcome with his brilliance.
ex.ja: 彼に会うたびごとに、彼の頭の良さに圧倒された。

note.ja: brilliant（輝かしい）+ -ance。イタリア語 brillare（輝く）。「輝き・優秀さ」。

en: Water in which food (meat, vegetable, etc.) has been boiled.
A soup made from broth and other ingredients such as vegetables, herbs or diced meat.

broth.ety: From Middle English broth, from Old English broþ (“broth”), from Proto-West Germanic *broþ (“broth”), from Proto-Germanic *bruþą (“broth”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰrewh₁- (“to seethe, roil, brew”). By surface analysis, brew + -th (abstract nominal suffix).

ex.en: The broth is hot.
ex.ja: そのスープ熱いよ。

ex.en: You're right. The noodle broth here is a bit expensive.
ex.ja: その通りさ。ここの麺の出汁はちょっと値が張るんだ。

ex.en: Too many cooks spoil the broth.
ex.ja: 料理人が多すぎるとスープができそこなう。

note.ja: 古英語 broth から。brew（醸造する）と同系。「スープ・だし」。

en: Occurring every 100 years.
Lasting or aged 100 years, 100-year-old.
Synonym of centennial: a hundredth anniversary.
Synonym of hundredweight, especially (historical) in Greek and Roman contexts.

note.ja: ラテン語 centenarius（100の）から。centum（100）。century と同じ。

en: A point or place where a check is performed, especially a point along a road or on a frontier where travellers are stopped for inspection.
A situation, often represented by a point in time, at which the state of a database system is known to be valid, and to which it can be r…
To set a checkpoint.

ex.en: There's a checkpoint at the border where they look in your trunk.
ex.ja: その国境には、トランクの中身を見るチェックポイントがある。

ex.en: The coalition force fired at her car at the checkpoint in Baghdad.
ex.ja: 同盟軍はバグダッドの検問所で彼女の車を襲撃した。

note.ja: check（検査）+ point（地点）。「検問所」。

en: Any binary compound of chlorine and another element or radical.
Any salt of hydrochloric acid.

chloride.ety: From chlor(ine) + -ide, coined by British chemist Humphry Davy in 1812.

note.ja: chlorine（塩素）+ -ide。「塩化物」。

en: to identify by or divide into classes; to categorize
to declare something a secret, especially a government secret

classify.ety: From French classifier. By surface analysis, class + -ify.

ex.en: Please classify these books by subject.
ex.ja: これらの本を主題別に分類してください。

ex.en: One can classify books into good ones and bad ones.
ex.ja: 本は良い物と悪い物とに分類できる。

ex.en: I classify his music as rock.
ex.ja: 私は彼の音楽をロックに入れる。

note.ja: class（分類）+ -ify。「分類する」→ 秘密の部類に入れる →「機密扱いにする（classified）」。

In the setting of a medical clinic; in a clinical setting; (of a health condition) to a degree high enough to be relevant to clinical pra…

en: Overly confident; arrogant and boastful.
A familiar name for a cockatoo.
To operate a small-scale farm.

cocky.ety: From cock (“male domestic chicken”) + -y (suffix forming adjectives with the sense of ‘having the quality of’).

ex.en: You cocky little kid!
ex.ja: 生意気な小僧がよ。

note.ja: cock（雄鶏）+ -y。雄鶏のように威張った →「生意気な」。

en: Cooperating.
A constant by which an algebraic term is multiplied.
An entry of a matrix.

coefficient.ety: From French coefficient. Coined by French mathematician François Viète. Or influenced by (New) Latin coefficient-, which is the stem of coefficiens, which is a substantivation of the present active participle of coefficio, which comes from co- and efficio.

note.ja: co（共に）+ efficient（作用する）。「共に作用するもの」→「係数」。

Hair conditioner.

ex.ja: エアコンの調子が悪い。

ex.ja: エアコンが空気を充分吸い込んでいない。

ex.en: This air conditioner uses a lot of electricity.
ex.ja: このエアコンは電気を食うな。

en: A cluster of heterogeneous things.
A corporation formed by the combination of several smaller corporations whose activities are unrelated to the corporation's primary activ…
Clustered together into a mass.
Composed of fragments of rock, pebbles, or stones cemented together.
To combine together into a larger mass.
To combine together into a larger corporation.

conglomerate.ety: First attested in the second part of the 16ᵗʰ century; from Latin conglomerātus, perfect passive participle of conglomerō (“to pile into a heap, to roll together”) (see -ate (Etymology 1, 2 and 3)), from con- (prefix indicating a being or bringing together of several objects) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱóm (“beside, by, near, with”)) + glomerāre (from glomerō (“to pile into a heap, to make into a ball, glomerate”), from glomus (“ball of thread; ball-shaped mass”), from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to form into a ball; ball”)).

note.ja: con（共に）+ glomus（球）+ -ate。「丸めて固めたもの」→「礫岩・複合企業」。

en: A stone forming the base at the corner of a building.
Such a stone used ceremonially, often inscribed with the architect's and owner's names, dates and other details.

cornerstone.ety: From Middle English corner ston; equivalent to corner + stone. The figurative sense is in part after Psalm 118:22, and is also quoted several times in the New Testament.

note.ja: corner（角）+ stone（石）。建物の角に置く最初の石 →「礎石・基礎」。

ja: 正しさ（political correctness：政治的妥当性）

en: Freedom from error.
Conformity to the truth or to fact.

ex.ja: その情報の正確さは、疑わしい。

en: False, especially of money; intended to deceive or carry appearance of being genuine.
Inauthentic.
A non-genuine article; a fake.
One who counterfeits; a counterfeiter.
To falsely produce what appears to be official or valid; to produce a forged copy of.
Of a turn or river card, to invalidate a player's hand by making a better hand on the board.

counterfeit.ety: From Middle English counterfeit, countrefet, from Anglo-Norman countrefait, from Old French contrefait, from Latin contra- (“against”) + Latin facere (“to make”). Piecewise doublet of contrafactum.

ex.en: The counterfeit bills flooded the market over the weekend.
ex.ja: 週末に偽札が市場にあふれた。

note.ja: counter（反対に・対応して）+ feit（作る）。ラテン語 contrafacere（まねて作る）から →「偽造の・偽物」。fac と同じ。

en: Extremely bright, especially so as to blind the eyes temporarily; bright to the degree that dazzles.
Very brilliant or splendid in display; that dazzles the mind of the observer.
The action of the verb to dazzle; dazzlement

ex.en: Your eyes are like corals, dazzling and very pretty.
ex.ja: 君の目はまるでサンゴのよう。ギラギラしていて、とてもきれい。

ex.en: The sun is dazzling.
ex.ja: 太陽がまぶしい。

ex.en: The noonday sun beat down with dazzling brightness on the tennis court.
ex.ja: 真昼の太陽がテニスコートを目も眩むほどに照らしあげた。

note.ja: dazzle（目をくらます）+ -ing。daze（ぼうっとさせる）と同系。「まばゆい」。

en: A designated minister of charity in the early Church (see Acts 6:1-6).
A clergyman ranked directly below a priest, with duties of helping the priests and carrying out parish work.
To ordain to the diaconate.
For a choir leader to lead a hymn by speaking one or two lines at a time, which are then sung by the choir.

deacon.ety: Inherited from Middle English deken, dekne, from Old English diacon, from Ecclesiastical Latin diāconus, from Ancient Greek διᾱ́κονος (diā́konos, “servant, minister”).

note.ja: ギリシャ語 diakonos（仕える者）から。「執事・助祭」。

en: To trick or mislead.

deceive.ety: From Middle English deceyven, from Anglo-Norman deceivre, from Latin dēcipiō (“to deceive; beguile; entrap”), from dē- (“from”) + capiō (“to seize”); see captive. Compare conceive, perceive, receive. Displaced native Old English beswīcan.

ex.en: Try it I think you will be deceived.
ex.ja: 騙されたと思ってやってみて。

ex.en: The boy I thought was honest deceived me.
ex.ja: 正直だと思っていた少年が私をだました。

ex.en: He is the last man to deceive me.
ex.ja: 彼は決して私をだますような人間ではない。

note.ja: de（離れて）+ ceiv（つかむ）+ e。（人の判断を）つかんで離さない →「だます・欺く」。deception（欺き）。

Operations performed on teeth and adjoining areas such as drilling, filling cavities, and placing crowns and bridges.

en: Someone who is detained, especially in custody or confinement.
Nervous, apprehensive.
Creatively challenging; cutting edge; leading edge.

edgy.ety: From edge + -y. Compare German eckig (“angular, edgy”).

ex.en: My boss is starting to get edgy.
ex.ja: 上司はいらいらしてきました。

en: A brief extra performance, done after the main performance is complete.
A call or demand (as by continued applause) for a repeat performance.
Please perform again!
To call for an extra performance or repetition of, or by.
To call for an encore.

encore.ety: Borrowed from French encore (“more, again”), and once used in this sense.

ex.en: Everyone called out to the singer for an encore.
ex.ja: 歌手に向かって盛んなアンコールが起こった。

ex.en: The pianist played two encores.
ex.ja: そのピアニストはアンコールに応えて２曲弾いた。

note.ja: フランス語で「もう一度」。英語では「アンコール」の意味で使う（フランスでは bis と言う）。

en: Extremely, greatly: to an enormous degree.
Shockingly.

enormously.ety:
Etymology tree
English enormous
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English enormously
From enormous + -ly.

ex.en: The economy of Japan has grown enormously.
ex.ja: 日本の経済は、大きく成長した。

ja: 誤る（To err is human：過ちは人の常）

en: To make a mistake.
To sin.
Elongated form of er (“sound of hesitation”).

err.ety: From Middle English erren, from Old French errer (“to wander, err, mistake”), from Latin errō (“wander, stray, err, mistake”, verb), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ers- (“to be angry, lose one's temper”). Cognate with Old English eorre, ierre (“anger, wrath, ire”), Old English iersian (“to be angry with, rage, irritate, provoke”), Old English ierre (“wandering, gone astray, confused”).

ex.en: He that thinks little, errs much.
ex.ja: あまり考えない者が、多くの過ちをおかす。

ex.en: He that talks much, errs much.
ex.ja: 多弁の人は多く誤る。

ex.en: He erred on the side of severity.
ex.ja: 彼は厳格すぎた。

note.ja: ラテン語 errare（さまよう・誤る）から。「誤る」。error、erratic と同じ。

en: To eject something violently (such as lava or water, as from a volcano or geyser).
To burst forth; to break out.

erupt.ety: From Latin eruptus, past participle of ērumpō (“to break out (of), to burst out (from)”), from e (“out”) + rumpō (“to break”).

ex.en: The volcano erupted suddenly, killing many people.
ex.ja: その火山は突然噴火し、多くの人が亡くなった。

ex.en: The volcano has erupted twice this year.
ex.ja: その火山は今年２度噴火した。

ex.en: The volcano may erupt at any moment.
ex.ja: その火山はいつなんどき爆発するかもしれない。

note.ja: e（外へ）+ rupt（破る）。破って外へ出る →「噴火する・爆発する」。

en: A concentrated coffee beverage brewed by forcing hot water under high pressure through finely ground coffee.
A drink that includes espresso as an ingredient.

espresso.ety:
Borrowed from Italian espresso, from caffè espresso (“pressed-out coffee”), form of esprimere (“to press out”), from Latin exprimere, from ex- (“out”) + primere (“to press”).
Some sources derive the term from "expressly" ("individually, directly") made for the customer, or from the Italian espresso ("fast"), as in the English word express ("fast"), although these explanations are not widely accepted. The original term for modern espresso (coffee extracted under pressure) was cream coffee, from Italian caffè crema (variant: crema caffè), due to the crema, and appeared on early Gaggia machines,

ex.en: An espresso doppio to drink inside.
ex.ja: エスプレッソドピオ店内で。

ex.en: I drank a very hot double espresso at the coffee shop this morning.
ex.ja: 今朝、コーヒーショップでとても熱いダブルエスプレッソを飲んだ。

note.ja: イタリア語 caffè espresso（押し出されたコーヒー）から。express と同じ。

en: To get away from by cunning; to avoid by using dexterity, subterfuge, address, or ingenuity; to cleverly escape from.
To escape; to slip away; — sometimes with from.

evade.ety: From Middle French évader, from Latin ēvādō (“to pass or go over; flee”), from ē (“out of, from”) + vādō (“to go; walk”). See also wade.

ex.en: Jack tried to evade paying his taxes.
ex.ja: ジャックは脱税しようとした。

ex.en: He was accused of evading tax.
ex.ja: 彼は脱税で非難された。

ex.en: We won't be able to evade punishment this time.
ex.ja: 今度は罰をまぬがれまい。

note.ja: e（外へ）+ vadere（行く）。「抜け出す」→「避ける」。evasion、invade と同じ。

en: Resembling a freak.
Incapable of producing results, useless; doomed not to be successful; not worth attempting.
Insignificant; frivolous.

futile.ety: Borrowed from Middle French futile, from Latin fūtilis.

ex.en: It isn't futile to go to university.
ex.ja: 大学へ行くことは無駄ではない。

note.ja: ラテン語 futilis（漏れやすい）から。fundere（注ぐ）の仲間。注いでもこぼれる →「無駄な・むなしい」。

en: The embryo of a seed, especially of a seed used as a cereal or grain. See Wikipedia article on cereal germ.
The small mass of cells from which a part of an organism develops, or a macroscopic but immature form of that part; a bud.
To germinate.

germ.ety: From Middle French germe, from Latin germen (“bud, seed, embryo”). Doublet of germen.

ex.en: Germs are too tiny for our eyes to see.
ex.ja: 細菌は小さすぎて我々の眼には見えない。

ex.en: This milk is free from germs.
ex.ja: この牛乳は殺菌してある。

ex.en: This chemical will prevent germs from breeding.
ex.ja: この化学薬品は細菌の繁殖を防ぐだろう。

note.ja: ラテン語 germen（芽・種）から。「芽」→「細菌・萌芽」。germinate（発芽する）と同じ。German（ドイツ人）とは別語。

en: Of, or relating to glaciers.
Very slow.
A glacial period (colloquially known as an ice age).

glacial.ety: Borrowed from French glacial, from Latin glaciālis, from glaciēs (“ice”). The sense "slow" refers to the speed of actual glaciers, typically around 1 meter per day.

ex.ja: 私は落ち込んでしまいあきらめようかと思った。

note.ja: gloom（薄暗さ・憂鬱）+ -y。「薄暗い・憂鬱な」。

ex.ja: 彼女は美しいが、さらによいことには非常に上品だ。

ex.ja: その婦人の態度はしとやかだ。

Existing only for certain seasons; that is, being dry for part of the year.

intermittent.ety: From Middle French intermittent, from Latin intermittens (“sending between”), from prefix inter- (“among, on”) + mittens (“sending”), from mittere (“to send”).

iteration.ety: From Latin iterātiō, from iterō. Morphologically iterate + -ion.

ex.ja: 彼は自分のすきな格言をいれた。

note.ja: ラテン語 maxima（最大の命題）から。max（最大）。最も重要な言葉 →「格言・金言」。

en: Black bile, formerly thought to be one of the four "cardinal humours" of animal bodies.

Affected with great sadness or depression.
Suggestive of wistfulness or subdued emotion.

melancholy.ety: From Middle English malencolie, from Old French melancolie, from Ancient Greek μελαγχολία (melankholía, “atrabiliousness”) (from μέλας (mélas), μελαν- (melan-, “black, dark, murky”) + χολή (kholḗ, “bile”)), referring to the humour which ancient Hippocratic and later Galenic medicine associated with sadness and despondency. ex.ja: 彼の声には憂鬱な調子が感じられた。

en: Of, or relating to a predator.
Living by preying on other living animals.

predatory.ety: Borrowed from Latin praedātōrius, equivalent to predator + -y.

note.ja: predator（捕食者）+ -y。ラテン語 praeda（獲物）。「捕食性の・食い物にする」。prey と同じ。

en: A beginning or introductory portion that comes before the main text of a document or book, typically serving to contextualize or explain …
An introduction, or series of preliminary remarks.
To introduce or make a comment before (the main point); to premise.
To give a preface to.

preface.ety: Late 14th century, from Middle English preface, prefas, from Old French preface (from which derives the modern French préface), from Medieval Latin prefātia, for classical Latin praefātiō (“a saying beforehand”), from praefor (“to speak beforehand”), from prae- (“beforehand”) + for (“to speak”).

ex.ja: 彼はその戯曲にすばらしい序文を書いた。

ex.en: He said a few words by way of preface.
ex.ja: 彼は前置きとして、すこし話した。

ex.en: How does the preface run?
ex.ja: 序文にはなんと書いてありますか。

note.ja: ラテン語 praefatio（前もって言うこと）から。prae + fari（話す）。「序文」。

To specify by writing as a required procedure or ritual; to lay down authoritatively as a guide, direction, or rule of action.

ex.ja: 抗生物質を処方しましょう。

en: Inflicting punishment; punishing.

punitive.ety: From Middle French punitif, from Medieval Latin pūnitīvus, from pūniō (“to punish”).

en: A forest in a climate with high annual rainfall and no dry season.

rainforest.ety: From rain + forest, a calque of German Regenwald.

ex.en: Rainforests provide the earth with many benefits.
ex.ja: 熱帯雨林は地球に多くの恩恵を与える。

ex.ja: 熱帯雨林の破壊は環境に影響を及ぼす。

ex.ja: マダガスカルの熱帯林の９０％以上が伐採されました。

note.ja: rain（雨）+ forest（森）。「熱帯雨林」。

en: Revived or regenerated, especially emotionally or spiritually.
Reincarnated.
A manufactured vinyl doll that has been transformed to resemble a human baby with as much realism as possible.

ex.ja: 生まれ変わったらカナダ人になりたい。

ex.ja: 生まれ変わったらヴァイオリン習いたい。

ex.ja: 赤茶色の屋根の建物は、教会だよ。

ex.ja: 彼女は赤味がかった髪の毛をしている。それで「にんじん」というあだながついている。

en: Rebuilt or replenished with all new material; or, restored to its original (or a better) working order and appearance.
A book, pamphlet or other printed matter that has been published once before but is now being released again.
To print (something) that has been published in print before.
To renew the impression of.

ex.en: Is it possible to reprint this article?
ex.ja: この記事を転載することは可能でしょうか。

ex.en: Is reprinting this article a possibility?
ex.ja: この記事を転載することは可能でしょうか。

note.ja: re（再び）+ print（印刷）。「増刷・再版」。

en: A room containing a public toilet: a public lavatory.

restroom.ety: From rest + room, from an earlier sense of "breakroom".

ex.en: Can you tell me where the restroom is?
ex.ja: お手洗いはどこか教えて下さいませんか。

ex.en: There was a long line for the women's restroom.
ex.ja: 女性用トイレは長蛇の列だった。

ex.en: There was a long line for the women's restrooms.
ex.ja: 女性用トイレは長蛇の列だった。

Characterized by rhythm.

From Ancient Greek ῥυθμικός (rhuthmikós), from ῥυθμός (rhuthmós, “measured flow or movement, symmetry, rhythm”) + -ικός (-ikós, suffix forming adjectives), equivalent to rhythm + -ic.

en: A game of chance in which a small ball is made to move round rapidly on a circle divided off into numbered (usually red and black) spaces…
An instance of risk-taking, especially when the downside exceeds the upside (contrary to the game of roulette where only the wager is lost).
To separate or decorate by incisions made with a small toothed wheel.

roulette.ety: Borrowed from French roulette (“roulette, little wheel”). The sense "situation with a random chance of incurring serious harm" may be abstracted from Russian roulette.

note.ja: フランス語 roulette（小さな車輪）から。rouelle（車輪）。ラテン語 rota。rotate と同じ。

en: Any of the monetary currencies used in modern India, Mauritius, Nepal, Pakistan, the Seychelles, or Sri Lanka.
A silver coin circulating in India between the 16th and 20th centuries, weighing one tola (formerly 170–180 troy grains; from 1833, 180 t…

rupee.ety: Coined by Sher Shah Suri, the Sultan of the Suri Empire 1540–1545 as Hindustani रुपीया / رُوپِییَہ (rūpīya), variant of रुपया / رُوپَیَہ (rūpaya, “rupee”), from Sanskrit रूप्यक (rūpyaka, “silver coin”), from रूप्य (rūpya, “wrought gold or silver; stamped coin; beautiful, well-shaped; impressed, stamped”). Doublet of rufiyaa and rupiah.

ex.en: The sentence got longer after it was re-written.
ex.ja: 文章を書き直して長くしました。

ex.en: If you’re a bad person, then it’s your problem.
ex.ja: あなたが悪い人なら、それはあなたの問題です。

ex.en: They’re going out together.
ex.ja: 彼らは付き合っている。

note.ja: サンスクリット語 rūpya（銀貨）から。

en: A cloth woven from silk, nylon or polyester with a glossy surface and a dull back. (The same weaving technique applied to cotton produces…
Semigloss.
To make (paper, silver, etc.) smooth and glossy like satin.

satin.ety: From French satin, which is derived from "Zaitun", the Arabic name for the Chinese city of Quanzhou, itself derived from Arabic زَيْتُون (zaytūn, “Zayton; olive”), from phono-semantic matching from Chinese 刺桐 (MC tshjeH duwng, “coral tree”) in 刺桐城 (MC tshjeH duwng dzyeng, “coral tree town”), an old name for Quanzhou.

ex.en: Is that a satin dress?
ex.ja: それがサテンのドレス？

ex.en: She was wearing a gown of satin.
ex.ja: 彼女は繻子のガウンを着ていた。

note.ja: アラビア語 zaitūnī（中国の泉州の）とされる。そこから輸出された絹織物 →「サテン」。

en: To (cause to) separate and go in different directions; to disperse.
To distribute loosely as by sprinkling.
The act of scattering or dispersing.
A collection of dispersed objects.

scatter.ety:
From Middle English scateren, skateren, also schateren,
* probably a variant of shatter, which is imitative;
* or from Old English *sceaterian, probably akin to a dialect of Old Norse, possibly ultimately related to Proto-Indo-European *skey- (“to cut, split, shatter”).
Compare Middle Dutch scheteren (“to scatter”), Low German schateren, Dutch schateren (“to burst out laughing”); and is apparently remotely akin to Ancient Greek σκεδάννυμι (skedánnumi, “scatter, disperse”). and Tocharian B kät- (“to scatter, sow seeds”). Doublet of shatter.

ex.en: Don't scatter your things about.
ex.ja: お前の物をその辺りに散らかすな。

ex.en: Sighing, each boy began to scatter.
ex.ja: ため息をつくと、男子たちは散っていった。

note.ja: 中英語 skateren から。shatter（粉々にする）と同系。「まき散らす」。

en: To move hurriedly to a location, especially by using all limbs against a surface.
To proceed to a location or an objective in a disorderly manner.
A rush or hurry, especially making use of the limbs against a surface.
An emergency defensive air force mission to intercept attacking enemy aircraft.
Shouted when something desirable is thrown into a group of people who individually want that item, causing them to rush for it.

scramble.ety: Origin uncertain. Perhaps from earlier dialectal scramble, scrammel (“to collect or rake together with the hands”), from scramb (“to pull or scrape together with the hands”) + -le (frequentative suffix) (compare Dutch schrammen (“to graze, brush, scratch”)); or alternatively from a nasalised form of scrabble (“to scrape or scratch quickly”).

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。scrabble（引っかき回す）と同系。「よじ登る・奪い合う」→ 卵をかき混ぜる。

en: Separated or isolated from others, or from another group.
Having access restricted to certain groups, or excluding certain groups.

ex.en: The buses in Montgomery were segregated.
ex.ja: モントゴメリーのバスは人種隔離が行われていた。

en: A branch of linguistics studying the meaning of words.
The study of the relationship between words and their meanings.

semantics.ety: From French sémantique + English -s, displacing earlier semasiology. The French is a learned borrowing from Ancient Greek σημαντικός (sēmantikós); see semantic. By surface analysis, semantic + -ics or semantic + -s.

note.ja: semantic + -s（学）。「意味論」。

ex.ja: 厚顔無恥とはまさにあいつのことだ。

ex.ja: 恥知らずな嘘つきは笑って嘘をいう。

A glimpse of something; a portrayal of something at a moment in time.
To take a photograph of.
To capture the state of, in a snapshot.

ex.ja: これは浜辺で撮った妻のスナップ写真です。

ex.ja: 今すぐバックアップを取った方がいいよ。

en: To fly high with little effort, like a bird.
To mount upward on wings, or as on wings, especially by gliding while employing rising air currents.
The act of soaring.
An upward flight.

soar.ety: From Middle English soren, from Old French essorer (“to fly up, soar”), from Vulgar Latin *exaurare (“to rise into the air”), from Latin ex (“out”) + aura (“the air, a breeze”), from Ancient Greek αὔρα (aúra, “breath”). Compare aura, and exhale.

ex.en: His stock with the students has soared.
ex.ja: 学生間では彼の株が急に上がった。

ex.en: The stock price index soared to an all-time high.
ex.ja: 株価指数は過去最高に上昇した。

ex.en: Prices have soared every year.
ex.ja: 物価は毎年上昇してきた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 essorer（空中に舞い上がる）から。ラテン語 ex + aura（空気）。「舞い上がる・急上昇する」。

en: Shaped as a sphere; being a sphere.
Of, or pertaining to, spheres.

spherical.ety: English spheric [from Latin sphaericus, from Ancient Greek σφαιρικός (sphairikós)] + -al.

ex.en: The child drew a spherical triangle.
ex.ja: あの子が球面三角を書きました。

note.ja: sphere（球）+ -ical。「球形の」。

en: To cause (a substance) to fall in fine drops (for a liquid substance) or small pieces (for a solid substance).
To cover (an object) by sprinkling a substance on to it.
A light covering with a sprinkled substance.
A light rain shower.

sprinkle.ety: From Middle English sprenkelen, sprynklen, from Middle Dutch sprenkelen, equivalent to sprink + -le (frequentative suffix). Cognate with Dutch sprenkelen (“to sprinkle”), German Low German sprenkeln (“to sprinkle; dapple”), German sprenkeln (“to sprinkle”).

ex.en: We sprinkle salt to ward off bad luck.
ex.ja: 縁起に塩をまいて清める。

ex.en: It's like sprinkling water on a desert.
ex.ja: 砂漠に水をまくようなものだ。

ex.en: She sprinkled some scent on her dress.
ex.ja: 彼女はドレスに香水を振り掛けた。

note.ja: 中英語 sprenkelen から。「振りかける」。sprinkler（散水装置）。

en: Any of various large coniferous evergreen trees or shrubs from the genus Picea, found in northern temperate and boreal regions; originall…
The wood of a spruce.
Smart, trim, and elegant in appearance; fastidious (said of a person).
To arrange neatly; tidy up.
To make oneself spruce (neat and elegant in appearance).

spruce.ety: From Middle English Spruce, an alteration of Pruce (“Prussia”), from Medieval Latin, from a Baltic language, probably Old Prussian; for more, see Prussia. Spruce, spruse (1412), and Sprws (1378) were terms for commodities brought to England by Hanseatic merchants (beer, wood, leather). The tree with this name was also believed to have been native to Prussia. The adjective and verb senses ("trim, neat" and "to make trim, neat") are attested from 1594, and originate with spruce leather (1466), which was used to make a popular style of jerkins in the 1400s that was considered smart-looking.

note.ja: Pruce（プロイセン）の変化形。プロイセンから来た木 →「トウヒ」、プロイセン製の革 →「こぎれいな」。

en: The energy and strength for continuing to do something over a long period of time; power of sustained exertion, or resistance to hardship…

stamina.ety: From Latin stāmina, plural of stāmen.

ex.en: I don't have the stamina needed to play sports like Tennis.
ex.ja: 私は体力がないので、テニスのようなスポーツができません。

ex.en: What you lack is stamina.
ex.ja: お前に足りないのは、持久力だよ。

ex.en: Sam doesn't have the stamina to finish a marathon.
ex.ja: サムにはマラソンを完走するだけの力がない。

note.ja: ラテン語 stamen（糸）の複数形。運命の女神が紡ぐ命の糸 →「生命力」→「スタミナ」。

The part of the mind that we are not normally aware of.

ex.en: Maybe the impulse was working upon her subconscious.
ex.ja: たぶん彼女の潜在意識の中にそういう衝動があったんでしょうね。

en: Pertaining to tension, especially of the muscles.
Restorative; curative; or invigorating.
A substance with medicinal properties intended to restore or invigorate.
Tonic water.

ex.en: What do you need to make gin and tonic?
ex.ja: ジントニックを作るには何がいるの？

ex.en: I'd like a vodka and tonic.
ex.ja: ウォッカ・トニックをください。

ex.en: I'd like a gin and tonic.
ex.ja: ジン・トニックをください。

en: Causing trouble or anxiety.

ex.en: It is the first step which is troublesome.
ex.ja: 厄介なのは最初の一歩だ。

ex.en: In any case, it's troublesome, isn't it?
ex.ja: どっちにしても、厄介ですね。

ex.en: We have to somehow come through this troublesome situation.
ex.ja: 我々はこの難局を何とかして切り抜けなければならない。

note.ja: trouble（困難）+ -some（〜を生じる）。「厄介な」。

en: Commonwealth standard spelling of tumor.

tumour.ety: From Middle English tumour, from Old French tumour, from Latin tumor (“swelling”), from tumeō (“bulge, swell”, verb), from Proto-Indo-European *tewh₂- (“to swell”). Related to English thumb.

ex.en: I have fibroid tumours. Is there a way to stop them getting large?
ex.ja: 子宮筋腫があります。大きくならないようにする方法はありますか？

note.ja: tumor のイギリスのつづり。

note.ja: トマス・モアの著書『ユートピア』（1516年）から。ギリシャ語 ou（ない）+ topos（場所）。「どこにもない場所」。

en: To become invisible or to move out of view unnoticed.
To become equal to zero.
The brief terminal part of a vowel or vocal element, differing more or less in quality from the main part.
A magic trick in which something seems to disappear.

vanish.ety:

ex.en: The tiger is a vanishing species.
ex.ja: 虎は消滅しかかっている種族である。

ex.en: We should try to be philosophical about life; wealth gained could also vanish.
ex.ja: 人生はあきらめが肝心。設けた財産も消えさることがありうるのだから。

note.ja: ラテン語 vanescere（空になる）から。van（空の）。→「消える・消滅する」。vain、vacant も同じ祖先。

en: A body of water, such as a river, channel or canal, that is navigable.
A conduit or watercourse, such as on the deck of a ship, to drain water.

waterway.ety: From Middle English waterwey, from Old English wæterweġ (“waterway”), from Proto-West Germanic *watarweg, equivalent to water + way. Compare Saterland Frisian Woaterwai (“waterway”), West Frisian wetterwei (“waterway”), Dutch waterweg (“waterway”), German Wasserweg (“waterway”), Danish vandvej (“waterway”), Swedish vattenväg (“waterway”).

ex.en: The waterways branch out across the plain.
ex.ja: 平野を横切って水路が枝分かれしている。

ex.en: The waterways ramify across the plain.
ex.ja: 平野を横切って水路が枝分かれしている。

note.ja: water（水）+ way（道）。「水路」。

en: Land that is covered mostly with water, with occasional marshy and soggy areas.

wetland.ety: From wet + land. Cognate with West Frisian wetlân.

note.ja: wet（湿った）+ land（土地）。「湿地」。

en: Without notice to prepare the mind for the event; sudden; hasty; unceremonious.
Curt in manner.
To interrupt suddenly.
Something which is abrupt; an abyss.

abrupt.ety: First attested in 1583. Borrowed from Latin abruptus (“broken off”), perfect passive participle of abrumpō (“break off”), formed from ab (“from, away from”) + rumpō (“to break”).

ex.en: The car came to an abrupt stop.
ex.ja: その車は急停車した。

ex.en: The car made an abrupt turn.
ex.ja: その車は不意に方向を変えた。

ex.en: Excuse me for the abrupt question.
ex.ja: つかぬことをお伺いします。

note.ja: ab（離れて）+ rupt（破る）。ちぎれ離れた →「突然の・ぶっきらぼうな」。

zh: 首字母縮略詞 /首字母缩略词

en: Generally such abbreviations, including those pronounced as individual letters (initialisms such as "TNT").
Exclusively such abbreviations when pronounced as a word (as "laser" or "NATO").
To form into an acronym.

acronym.ety: Borrowed from German Akronym (from Ancient Greek ἄκρον (ákron, “end; peak”) + ὄνυμα (ónuma, “name”)), modelled after Homonym and Synonym, first attested in German in the early 1900s and in English in 1940. By surface analysis, acro- (prefix meaning ‘beginning; high’) + -onym (suffix meaning ‘name’)

note.ja: ギリシャ語 akron（先端）+ onyma（名前）。「頭の文字でできた名前」→「頭字語」。acrobat（つま先で歩く人）と同じ akro。

en: The state of adverse conditions; state of misfortune or calamity.
An event that is adverse; calamity.

adversity.ety: From Old French adversité, from Latin adversitātem, the accusative singular of adversitās, from adversus, the perfect passive participle of advertō (“to turn toward”).

ex.en: Adversity makes a man wise, not rich.
ex.ja: 艱難汝を玉にす。

ex.en: Adversity is the best school.
ex.ja: 逆境で人は成長する。

ex.en: They must have struggled against adversity from their early days.
ex.ja: 彼らは幼い時から逆境と闘ってきたにちがいない。

note.ja: ad（〜に）+ vers（向ける）+ ity。（運が）こちらに背を向けること →「逆境・不運」。

en: A signed document wherein an affiant makes a sworn statement.
To swear by such a document.

affidavit.ety: From Medieval Latin affidavit (“he has sworn”), the third person singular perfect tense of affido (“swear”), from fīdō, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeydʰ- (“to command, to persuade, to trust”). Cognate to fidelity and faith (same Latin root), but not to affirm (shared Latin ad- prefix, but different Latin and Proto-Indo-European roots).

note.ja: 中世ラテン語で「彼は誓った」。affidare（誓う）。「宣誓供述書」。fidelity と同じ fid。

en: Divination about human affairs or natural phenomena from the relative positions of celestial bodies.

astrology.ety: From Middle French astrologie, and its source, Latin astrologia (“astronomy”), from Ancient Greek ἀστρολογία (astrología, “telling of the stars”), from ἄστρον (ástron, “star, planet, or constellation”) + -λογία (-logía, “treating of”), a combination form of -λόγος (-lógos, “one who speaks (in a certain manner)”). ex.en: Are you interested in astrology?
ex.ja: 星占いに興味ある？

ex.en: What's the difference between astronomy and astrology?
ex.ja: 天文学と占星学とは何が違うでしょう？

note.ja: astr（星）+ o + log（学問）+ y。星の学問 →「占星術」。astronomy（天文学）と区別。

The total mass of all, or a specified category of, living things within a specific area, habitat, etc.

en: A shirt for women or girls, particularly a shirt with buttons and often a collar; a dress shirt tailored for women.
A loose-fitting uniform jacket.
To hang a garment in loose folds.
To tuck one's pants/trousers (into one's boots).

1828, from French blouse (“a workman's or peasant's smock”), see that for more.

ex.ja: 彼女はそのブラウスをすばやく洗った。

ex.ja: 彼女は赤いブラウスを着た。

note.ja: フランス語 blouse（仕事着）から。語源ははっきりしない。

To act as bodyguard for (someone).
To protect (someone or something).

ex.en: What I need is a bodyguard.
ex.ja: 私に必要なのは、ボディガードです。

ex.ja: トムには個人的なボディガードがいる。

ex.ja: ボディーガードは、イヤホンをしていた。

note.ja: body（体）+ guard（守る人）。「ボディーガード」。

en: One who borrows.

borrower.ety: From Middle English borower, borewer, borwere, equivalent to borrow + -er (agent suffix).

ex.en: Banks are cutting lending to industrial borrowers.
ex.ja: 銀行は産業向け貸出を減らしている。

note.ja: borrow（借りる）+ -er。「借り手」。

en: A branch of biology concerned with the scientific study of plants.
The plant life of a geographical area; flora.

botany.ety: First attested in 1696: Back-formation from botanic.

ex.en: Botany is the scientific study of plants.
ex.ja: 植物学とは植物の科学的研究のことである。

ex.en: Botany deals with the study of plants.
ex.ja: 植物学は植物の研究を扱っている。

ex.en: Zoology and botany deal with the study of life.
ex.ja: 動物学と植物学は生命の研究を取り扱っている。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 botanē（草・牧草）から。boskein（家畜に草を食べさせる）。「植物学」。

A vehicle with a caterpillar track; a crawler.
To move along slowly, drawing one's body up, in the manner of a caterpillar.

Displaced native kaleworm, from Middle English cowle worm, cale worme (“caterpillar, corn weevil”), from Old English cawelwyrm, cawelwurm (“caterpillar”).

The sound of talking.
To talk idly.
To make a noise by rapid collisions.

A spellcaster class that receives their spells (especially healing) from their deity.
Of or pertaining to the clergy.

An instrument for compressing an artery (especially the femoral artery) or other part.

To talk together, to consult, discuss; to collogue.

ex.ja: あなたはこの問題を弁護士に相談するべきです。

cougar.ety: From French couguar, from Portuguese cuguardo, a deformation of Brazilian Portuguese suçuarana (earlier çuçuarana), from Old Tupi sûasuarana.

note.ja: トゥピ語（南米）に由来する。「ピューマ」。

(said of a sequence or series) Diverging; not approaching a limit.

divergent.ety: From Latin dis- (“apart”) + vergere (“to turn”) + the adjectival suffix -ent.

ex.ja: 彼女は博士号を取得した。

Absolute, complete.
Of a person or their behaviour: direct, plain, straightforward; also, of speech: direct and unambiguous; blunt, to the point.

ex.en: The girl was not downright homely.
ex.ja: その女の子はひどく不美人というほどではなかった。

ex.en: That movie's downright dirty.
ex.ja: あの映画はえげつない。

note.ja: down（下まで）+ right（まっすぐ）。「まっすぐ下まで」→「まったく」。

A collector or emitter of electric charge in a semiconducting device.

Basic, fundamental or elementary.
A creature (usually a spirit) that is attuned with, or composed of, one of the classical elements: air, earth, fire and water or variatio…

note.ja: element（要素）+ -al。「基本的な・自然の力の」。

To promote (someone) to a higher rank.

ex.ja: 新しい心理と知識は、常に人間生活を向上させ、たいてい実際に利用されるようになる。

Talkative and sociable.

ex.ja: こんな広大な景色は初めて見ました。

A scale of a fish or similar animal
To break or chip off in a flake.
To prove unreliable or impractical; to abandon or desert, to fail to follow through.

ex.en: Corn flakes and milk certainly go well together.
ex.ja: 確かに牛乳とコーンフレークの相性は抜群だ。

ex.en: Snow fell in large flakes.
ex.ja: 大きな雪片がひらひらと降った。

en: An exclamation denoting surprise or frustration.

geez.ety: A minced oath from the word Jesus.

ex.en: Geez, I wish this test would finish soon.
ex.ja: はーあ、早くテスト終わってくんないかなあ。

ex.en: "... in other words, sex!?" "Geez, you don't beat around the bush!"
ex.ja: 「・・・つまり、セックス！？」「うわあ、健二ったら・・・みもふたもない」

ex.en: Geez - I'm getting nervous.
ex.ja: やべー緊張してきたわ。

note.ja: Jesus を婉曲に言った間投詞。gee と同じ。
